study.hypothesis: After agent-authored code first entered Counterfact's main branch, development output would increase without worsening the rate of newly introduced externally reported defects, report-to-release time, or automated test coverage.
study.design: Retrospective observational self-audit; the hypothesis was formulated after the observation period and was not preregistered.

intervention.basis: First agent-authored product change merged into the main branch.

matureWindows.definition: Releases and external reports enter from the cohort start through June 6 at 00:00 UTC; every included record is then followed for exactly 90 days through September 4 at 00:00 UTC.

primaryOutcomes: Raw count of externally reported product defects first released by June 6 and reported within 90 days; rate denominators are sensitivity analyses.
Kaplan-Meier time to first public corrected release for reports entering by June 6, administratively censored at 90 days.
Automated test-file count, explicit test declarations, and reported branch coverage at the pre-adoption and end-of-observation snapshots.

retrospectiveComparison.ordinaryMeasureRule: Use the median and observed range of every pre-AI cohort with a complete comparable measurement.
retrospectiveComparison.introducedDefectRule: Pool qualifying cases whose external report and first affected public release both entered the cohort window, along with non-dependency merged pull requests, across every eligible pre-AI cohort; then apply that rate to the observed 2026 exposure.
retrospectiveComparison.coverageRule: Treat the midpoint of the two complete pre-AI coverage changes as a descriptive reference, not a forecast.
retrospectiveComparison.interpretation: Descriptive historical baselines, not prospective predictions, prediction intervals, causal estimates, or estimates of what necessarily would have happened without AI.

populationRules.include: Public issue or accepted standalone pull request opened in the window by a human external author and describing confirmed faulty product behavior.
populationRules.deduplicate: A pull request linked to an included issue is evidence for that issue, not a second report.
populationRules.process: Release-integrity and workflow failures are recorded separately from product defects.

productCases.title: Optional properties become required when their nested schemas contain required properties
productCases.shortTitle: Nested schemas made optional properties required
productCases.originSummary: The schema encoder began deciding optionality from the child schema’s own required array instead of the parent object’s required list.
productCases.failure: A property omitted from its parent schema’s required list was emitted without a TypeScript optional marker when that property’s nested object had required children.
productCases.finding: The responsible condition entered the generator in 2022 and is present in releases well before the 2025 boundary. No 2026 change created the behavior.
productCases.historyEvidence: Rename-aware history traces the faulty required-property check to the 2022 schema-type encoder implementation. The fix changes that decision to use the parent object’s required list and adds the reporter’s nested-object shape as a test.
productCases.releaseEvidence: The origin commit is contained in 0.8.0; the accepted fix shipped in 2.0.0 one day after the report.

productCases.title: Root middleware is not executed
productCases.originSummary: A recursive middleware lookup stopped when it reached the empty root path instead of performing the existing '/' registry lookup.
productCases.failure: Middleware placed at the route root was skipped, although the same middleware ran when placed under a subroute.
productCases.finding: The empty-string-versus-slash mismatch was introduced in February 2025 and released in 1.3.0. It remained present through the version named by the reporter.
productCases.historyEvidence: The February 14 recursion change replaced the explicit '/' lookup and returned when the remaining path became empty. A later commit changed the recursion terminal value but did not create the behavior. The fix restores a normalized root lookup and includes a root-level middleware test.
productCases.releaseEvidence: The faulty commit first appears in 1.3.0. The correction shipped in 2.2.0, 17 calendar days after the report—the only 2026 product case that took more than five days to reach a release.

productCases.title: Invalid operationId characters generate invalid TypeScript identifiers
productCases.shortTitle: Invalid operation IDs broke generated TypeScript
productCases.originSummary: The new operationId-based export feature used punctuation-bearing operation identifiers verbatim as TypeScript identifiers.
productCases.failure: Operation IDs containing characters that TypeScript identifiers cannot contain produced generated source that failed to parse.
productCases.finding: The capability and defect shipped together in 2.0.0. The external contributor reported and fixed the defect directly in an accepted pull request rather than opening a separate issue.
productCases.historyEvidence: The operationId export implementation introduced the verbatim identifier. PR #1516 adds identifier sanitization and focused coverage; a maintainer approved it and all required checks passed before merge.
productCases.releaseEvidence: The feature and defect first shipped in 2.0.0. The accepted contributor fix shipped later on the report date in 2.0.1.
productCases.nuance: This record is why the population includes accepted standalone external defect pull requests. Counting only issues would omit a real public report merely because its author supplied the repair at the same time.

productCases.title: Reserved-keyword operationId values generate invalid TypeScript
productCases.shortTitle: Reserved operation IDs broke generated TypeScript
productCases.originSummary: The new operationId-based type-export feature used identifiers such as 'delete' verbatim in generated imports and type declarations.
productCases.failure: An OpenAPI operation whose operationId was a TypeScript reserved word produced source that could not be parsed.
productCases.finding: The applicable capability—operation-specific exports named from operationId—first shipped in 2026 and contained the defect in its initial release. There was no earlier working version of that feature to regress from.
productCases.historyEvidence: The failure begins with the operationId export implementation merged through contributor-authored PR #1502. The repair aliases unsafe generated names while preserving the public operation identifier and adds reserved-word coverage.
productCases.releaseEvidence: The feature and defect first shipped together in 2.0.0. The fix shipped in 2.5.0 the day after the report.
productCases.nuance: This is one of two bugs attributable to code introduced in 2026. Calling it a feature defect is more precise than calling it a regression: the newly introduced behavior never had a working released state. The contribution passed project review, so authorship identifies provenance, not exclusive responsibility.

productCases.title: A response without a schema breaks generated type definitions
productCases.originSummary: A response-content refactor assumed that every media type supplied a schema and dereferenced the missing value.
productCases.failure: A valid response content entry with examples but no schema caused the generator to emit only an error comment instead of a useful operation type.
productCases.finding: The unsafe dereference dates to 2022. In the audit’s year-based taxonomy, this old regression is still pre-existing in 2025.
productCases.historyEvidence: Source history identifies the 2022 response-type refactor that introduced the unconditional schema access. The fix falls back to unknown and tests generation from content without a schema.
productCases.releaseEvidence: The faulty implementation appears in 0.13.0; the accepted fix shipped in 2.5.0 one day after the report.

productCases.title: Routes containing colons generate incorrect type-import paths
productCases.shortTitle: Colon routes produced the wrong import path
productCases.originSummary: A Windows-path compatibility change sanitized the generated filename but did not apply the same transformation to the route file’s type import.
productCases.failure: For a path such as /stuff:action, the generated type filename used a Unicode ratio character while the import retained a literal colon, leaving the handler argument typed as any.
productCases.finding: This was a genuine regression, but it occurred in September 2025 rather than 2026.
productCases.historyEvidence: The introducing change and the later fix are symmetrical: one transformed the output filename; the other made the generated import use the same safe-path function. The fix includes the colon-route reproduction.
productCases.releaseEvidence: The mismatch first shipped in 1.4.5. It was corrected in 2.5.0 one day after the report.

productCases.title: Non-operation Path Item fields cause a generator TypeError
productCases.shortTitle: Path Item metadata crashed the generator
productCases.originSummary: The original path traversal treated every Path Item key as an HTTP operation instead of filtering metadata fields such as summary and description.
productCases.failure: Standards-defined Path Item metadata was passed into operation generation, producing a TypeError when the generator searched a string for operationId.
productCases.finding: The loop’s assumption existed from the early generator implementation in 2022 and remained unchanged at the end of 2025.
productCases.historyEvidence: Historical source shows an unfiltered Object.entries traversal from 2022. The fix limits generation to supported HTTP methods and adds summary, description, servers, and parameters as regression fixtures.
productCases.releaseEvidence: The responsible traversal is present by 0.5.0. The fix shipped in 2.8.1 the next day.

productCases.title: Object-valued query parameters do not use OpenAPI’s exploded form
productCases.shortTitle: Exploded object query parameters were not assembled
productCases.originSummary: The earliest confirmed OpenAPI-aware query conversion still exposed the web framework’s flat query object and did not assemble form-exploded object parameters under their declared name.
productCases.failure: A request such as ?page=0&size=100 did not populate $.query.pageable and, once request validation existed, was rejected as missing the required pageable parameter.
productCases.finding: Request validation made the mismatch more visible in 2026, but it did not create the underlying deserialization omission. The same exploded input could not have produced the declared object in 2025.
productCases.historyEvidence: The flat query assignment is already present when OpenAPI-aware parameter conversion shipped in 0.13.1 and persists through the 2025 boundary. The later TypeScript conversion preserved rather than introduced it. The fix adds OpenAPI style/explode-aware assembly to both validation and handler input.
productCases.releaseEvidence: The omission is confirmed in 0.13.1; the audit does not claim that commit is the exact first possible origin. Correct exploded-object support shipped in 2.10.0 four days after the report.
productCases.nuance: This is the clearest latent-defect case. A new validator changed the symptom from incorrectly shaped handler data to a visible 400 response, but the supported OpenAPI serialization could not be consumed correctly before the validator existed either. Under the audit rules, increased visibility is not a new regression.

productCases.title: Path-level parameters are ignored
productCases.originSummary: Parameter collection read only operation-level arrays and never merged parameters declared on the enclosing Path Item.
productCases.failure: A path parameter declared once at path level was absent from generated handler types and unavailable to runtime parameter handling.
productCases.finding: The omission is visible in the earliest parameter-generation implementation from 2022 and remained present through 2025.
productCases.historyEvidence: Historical source consistently reads operation.parameters without incorporating pathItem.parameters. The fix merges both scopes with the OpenAPI-required operation-level override semantics and covers generator and runtime behavior.
productCases.releaseEvidence: The omission exists by 0.5.0. The correction shipped in 2.11.0 five days after the report.

productCases.title: Published package runs an obsolete patch-package postinstall hook
productCases.shortTitle: The package ran an obsolete postinstall hook
productCases.originSummary: A maintenance change accidentally restored patch-package as a production dependency and postinstall script after the package no longer shipped patches.
productCases.failure: Installing Counterfact invoked an unnecessary lifecycle script, creating avoidable friction for package managers with strict build-script policies and an unnecessary supply-chain concern.
productCases.finding: Published package manifests show the hook from 0.39.0 onward, including 2025 releases; no 2026 change introduced it.
productCases.historyEvidence: Package history traces the reintroduced script to a 2024 lint-maintenance commit. Inspection of published manifests corroborates that affected packages had the hook but no patches directory. The fix removes the dependency, script, and obsolete CI step.
productCases.releaseEvidence: The hook first shipped in 0.39.0. Its removal reached 2.12.0 one day after the report.

productCases.title: Generated context types expose $.header instead of $.headers
productCases.shortTitle: The generated context used the wrong headers property
productCases.originSummary: The early generated response-builder context declared a singular header property while runtime context exposed headers.
productCases.failure: TypeScript rejected the runtime-supported $.headers property and suggested a nonexistent singular $.header property instead.
productCases.finding: The mismatch is present years before the 2025 report. The cited release is a confirmed affected bound, not a claim that no earlier package was affected.
productCases.historyEvidence: History traces the singular generated declaration to the early response-builder type. The accepted fix changes only the generated name and the release note explicitly identifies #1160.
productCases.releaseEvidence: The audit confirms the mismatch by 0.8.0 and in the reporter's 1.1.5. The fix shipped in 1.1.6 two calendar days after the report.

productCases.title: Swagger UI cannot resolve references in external YAML files
productCases.shortTitle: External YAML references broke Swagger UI
productCases.originSummary: The documented OpenAPI viewer served the root document without bundling sibling-file references for the browser.
productCases.failure: A valid multi-file OpenAPI document worked as one file but displayed unresolved-reference errors in Counterfact's Swagger UI.
productCases.finding: The serving path is confirmed to preserve external references well before 2025. The audit does not claim the extraction commit was the first possible occurrence.
productCases.historyEvidence: The 2023 middleware state serves the document without producing a self-contained browser payload. The accepted fix bundles external references and reproduces the multi-file report in tests.
productCases.releaseEvidence: The behavior is confirmed by 0.29.0 and at the 2025 report. The eventual correction shipped in 2.2.1, 357 days after the report.

productCases.title: JSON response shortcuts require an exact content-type key
productCases.shortTitle: Content-type parameters hid the JSON shortcut
productCases.originSummary: The early response-builder shortcut type matched media types exactly rather than recognizing parameters such as charset.
productCases.failure: A response declared as application/json; charset=utf-8 did not expose the generated .json() convenience method.
productCases.finding: The exact-match type predates 2025. PR #1372 is counted with its linked issue, not as a second external report.
productCases.historyEvidence: The old conditional type requires exact key membership. The external contributor's accepted fix switches to a contains match; a later release reverted it and a separate 2026 repair restored the behavior.
productCases.releaseEvidence: The exact-match behavior is confirmed by 0.8.0. The initial fix shipped in 1.4.2 six days after the report.

productCases.title: OpenAPI paths containing colons create invalid Windows filenames
productCases.originSummary: Route-to-file generation used URL path text as filename text without a Windows-safe transformation.
productCases.failure: A valid route such as /stuff:action could not be generated on Windows because colons are forbidden in filenames.
productCases.finding: The filename scheme is confirmed affected years before the report. The precise earliest affected package is bounded rather than asserted beyond the available tagged comparison.
productCases.historyEvidence: The long-standing route filename scheme retained the colon. The fix introduces one Windows-safe transformation and adds a colon-bearing OpenAPI route to black-box and generator coverage.
productCases.releaseEvidence: The behavior is confirmed by 0.10.3 and in the reported 1.4.2. The fix shipped in 1.4.5 three calendar days after the report.

featureTimeline.title: An HTTP client inside the REPL
featureTimeline.detail: Developers could send requests to the simulated API without leaving the interactive session, alongside delay controls for latency testing.

featureTimeline.title: An Admin API and agent skill
featureTimeline.detail: Counterfact exposed a control surface intended for tooling and coding-agent workflows, while preserving the human-facing REPL.

featureTimeline.title: Request validation and a fluent request builder
featureTimeline.detail: Incoming requests could be checked against the OpenAPI contract, and route() added typed discovery, construction, autocomplete, and execution inside the REPL.

featureTimeline.title: Composable scenarios and startup state
featureTimeline.detail: Named scenario functions made state transitions reusable; startup scenarios could seed a useful simulated world automatically when the server began.

featureTimeline.title: Multiple APIs in one process
featureTimeline.detail: ApiRunner isolated generation and runtime state per specification and enabled grouped APIs to share one Counterfact server and REPL.

featureTimeline.title: First-class API versioning
featureTimeline.detail: Version-aware generated types, derived prefixes, and $.minVersion() let handlers be shared safely across versions of an API.

featureTimeline.title: OpenAPI 3.2 and Overlay support
featureTimeline.detail: QUERY, querystring parameters, streaming and server-sent events expanded protocol coverage; repeatable overlays made it possible to adapt a source document without editing it.

featureTimeline.title: A shared store and modular public packages
featureTimeline.detail: A typed, hot-reload-safe store became available to routes and tooling, while focused OpenAPI, generator, runtime, client, and REPL packages opened Counterfact to embedding and reuse.
